title: One station from the archive
prompt: The weather archive keeps one folder per station, and the New York desk only needs `NYC-01`. Write `load_nyc(path)` so it reads just that station's folder and returns its readings with `station_id` still in them. `solve` is written for you.
rules: Read only the `NYC-01` folder of the archive at `path`; there is always one.
Return the readings with every column: the others in their order, then `station_id` last.
Keep the readings as they are, missing values, `NaN` and `-9999` codes included.
Readings of other stations, even ones with similar names, are not returned.
hints: A partition's folder is named `column=value`, so this one is `station_id=NYC-01` inside `path`.
Reading one partition's folder leaves out the partition column, because it isn't stored in the files.
The `basePath` option tells Spark where the table starts, so it adds `station_id` back.
explanation: `spark.read.option("basePath", path).parquet(path + "/station_id=NYC-01")` opens only New York's folder, and `basePath` makes Spark treat `station_id=NYC-01` as a partition of the table at `path`, so the column comes back, last. Without `basePath` the result has no `station_id` at all. Reading the whole archive returns every station, and a pattern like `station_id=NYC-01*` also picks up a station called `NYC-010`.
